cohort: 191 HIV-seropositive pregnant women who delivered at the Regional Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS) between January 2007 and December 2011 and whose pregnancies were beyond 28 weeks gestation.
finding: The overall prevalence of HIV seropositivity among pregnant women delivering at RIMS was 0.41%, with the highest rate in 2007 (0.64%) and a decreasing trend over the study period.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was more common than cesarean delivery among HIV-seropositive women (71.2% vs. 28.8%).
